title: Manifold Grace synthetic cross-representational claim relationship test pack
license_notice: Synthetic examples created for educational assessment; not real institutional facts, legal advice, or scientific findings.
usage: Test claim relation classification, uncertainty recognition and justifications; verify case schemas separately before training or formal benchmarking.

labels.contradiction: Same scope and referent, incompatible claims.
labels.compatible_temporal: Claims potentially both true at different time points.
labels.not_entailment: One claim does not justify the other.
labels.evidence_gap: A relevant source required for adjudication is unavailable.
labels.dependency_review: A change to a source claim requires downstream reassessment.
labels.compatible_probabilistic: Stated probability and single observed outcome are compatible.
labels.insufficient_context: Identity or scope ambiguity blocks confident comparison.

source_a.claim: The committee approved the plan on 4 March 2026.

source_b.claim: The committee did not approve the plan on 4 March 2026.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Same decision, same date, opposing assertions.

source_b.claim: The service was discontinued in July 2025.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Both can be correct at different times.

source_a.claim: The system performs well on a coding benchmark.

source_b.claim: The system fails to generalise across legal tasks.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Benchmark performance is not all-domain intelligence.

source_a.claim: In 2024, analysts forecast a launch in 2027.

source_b.claim: A 2026 report says the product has not launched yet.

scenarios.reference_rationale: A forecast does not assert completed launch.

source_a.claim: A draft is labelled formally checked.

source_b.claim: The entire paper is scientifically novel.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Formal checking does not prove novelty.

source_a.claim: The record references an attached assessment.

source_b.claim: No assessment attachment is present in the supplied bundle.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Missing attachment limits verification of the assessment.

source_a.claim: The appeal was submitted on 11 April.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Paraphrases describe the same event and date.

source_a.claim: The policy required two signatures in 2023.

source_b.claim: The revised policy requires one signature from 2025.

source_a.claim: The first system finished in 10 minutes.

source_b.claim: The second system used half the total compute.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Elapsed time and compute are different measures.

source_a.claim: Claim B relies on theorem A.

source_b.claim: The proof of theorem A was withdrawn.

scenarios.reference_rationale: The dependent claim needs re-evaluation, not automatic falsification.

source_a.claim: High participation correlated with improved outcomes.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Correlation does not alone establish causation.

source_a.claim: The diagram places box X to the left of box Y.

source_b.claim: Box X necessarily caused box Y.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Spatial sequence does not prove causation.

source_a.claim: A model gives an event a 70% chance.

source_b.claim: The event did not occur in one observed case.

scenarios.reference_rationale: One non-occurrence does not falsify a calibrated 70% forecast.

source_a.claim: The provider acknowledged receipt of the proposal.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Receipt is not proof of adoption.

source_a.claim: The assessment was completed on 8 May.

source_b.claim: A separate assessment was completed on 9 May.

scenarios.reference_rationale: Cannot infer a date contradiction without confirming same assessment.
